subject: NYC traffic spillover - request for geo rehome and exec approval
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@nyc-retail.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@nyc-retail.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 08:04:00 -0400
Subject: URGENT: spike in 5xx and latency for NYC region

Connor —

We're seeing a sustained spike in p50/p95 latency and a 502/503 surge across our NYC footprint starting ~07:30 ET. Throughput into our inference endpoints dropped ~40% and error rate jumped to ~6–8% for user-facing requests. This started impacting checkout flows for our storefront (live traffic).

Attached is a short screenshot of the latency chart and a CSV of sample request IDs. Can you confirm:
- Is this on Redwood's side or a networking flap on our end?
- Can you trigger any cross-region reroute or protective throttle while you investigate?

We need an immediate mitigation (either a traffic steer or a fallback) — this is P0 for us. Please loop in whoever needed.

Thanks,
Nora Patel
Head of Platform Operations
NYC Retail
(attachment: latency_chart_q1.png)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@nyc-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 08:27:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: spike in 5xx and latency for NYC region — escalation and ask

Team — forwarding Nora's note. Summary: NYC region is experiencing a latency and error surge causing throughput collapse for an active customer (NYC Retail, high priority). Nora asked for an immediate reroute/fallback.

Quick context: customer is on Redwood Dedicated with regional pinning to us-east-1/NYC AZs. We've seen similar transient KV-cache warmups during cross-region moves but this looks larger (5–8% 5xx sustained). Attached: nyc_metric_snapshot_0728.json (short metrics export).

Asks:
- Can infra run an emergency geo rehome to us-east-2 (or us-east-1 -> us-east-2) for this customer's routes?
- If we activate a geo reroute, it needs exec sign-off for a one-time credit and customer's SLA exception.

Nora — we'll keep you in the loop; marking incident INC-20270728-NYC. Please expect an update in 15–30m.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
(attachment: nyc_metric_snapshot_0728.json)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@nyc-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: spike in 5xx and latency for NYC region — escalation and ask

Thanks for the quick ping, Connor.

I authorize the emergency geo-fallback to protect the customer's user experience, conditional on:
1) A short rollback trigger window if error rate increases after the move.
2) A clear communications note to the customer with estimated timeframe.
3) Incident ticket with timeline (INC-20270728-NYC).

Markus — please prepare the routing flip plan and call out KV cache warmup impact and any read-only degradation windows. Vanessa — prepare a short customer comms and confirm who on the CS side will be the post-change contact. Rishi — please advise on one-time credit/exception — what can be approved now so we don't block the mitigation.

I'll stay on this through the change and sign off on exec-level items.

— Hannah
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@nyc-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: spike in 5xx and latency for NYC region — routing plan

On Wed, Jul 28, 2027 at 08:04 AM Nora Patel <nora@nyc-retail.com> wrote:
> Connor —
>
> We're seeing a sustained spike...

Planned play:
- Step 1 (09:25 ET): test 10% traffic rehome to us-east-2 (metric checks at +2m, +5m).
- Step 2 (09:33 ET): if stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 10 minutes.
- Step 3: monitor KV hit ratio and warmup metrics; expect short-term p95 bump for ~5–15 minutes as KV caches rebuild.

Notes: us-east-2 pool has available capacity on dedicated nodes for this customer. We will execute a route patch (route_patch_v1.sh) and keep the previous route pinned for immediate rollback. Estimated execution window: 8–12m to reach 100% (if no blockers).

Risk: cross-region routing will increase tail latency briefly for cache-heavy workloads; we should throttle non-critical background jobs on the customer's tenant during the move if possible.

I'll run the patch at 09:25 ET pending Rishi approval on credits and Hannah sign-off (this email).

— Markus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: route_patch_v1.sh)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@nyc-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Approval: geo rehome + customer credit (NYC Retail)

Approved: authorize the geo rehome now.

Credit guidance: pre-approve a 10% one-time service credit for the customer's monthly invoice to be applied once we close the incident. Keep ledger of minutes/impact for any upsell/renewal conversation. If the customer requests a larger credit, escalate to finance and CS leads.

Connor — please confirm comms and credit application once incident is closed. Markus — proceed with the routing patch at the planned window and report back on completion and monitoring.

— Rishi
Director, Customer Success & Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Nora Patel <nora@nyc-retail.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: URGENT: spike in 5xx and latency for NYC region — follow-up

Team —

Thanks — I can confirm the customer saw normalized latency and error rate reductions after the move. Checkout throughput is back to baseline and we haven't observed residual 5xx spikes for the last 3 hours. Appreciate the rapid coordination.

Request: please share the postmortem and the credit confirmation so we can close our internal incident. Also would like a short note on steps you took and the timeline for our execs.

Nora Patel
Head of Platform Operations
NYC Retail
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora@nyc-retail.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: URGENT: spike in 5xx and latency for NYC region — follow-up and next steps

Nora — great to hear. We'll produce a one-page executive timeline and a brief postmortem and share the credit application (10% one-time) by EOD.

Summary (high level):
- 2027-07-28 07:30 ET: onset of elevated 5xx and p95 latency for NYC region.
- 2027-07-28 09:25 ET: initiated 10% test reroute to us-east-2; monitored at +2m/+5m.
- 2027-07-28 09:35 ET: ramped to 100% after stability checks; KV caches warmed over ~10 minutes.
- 2027-07-28 09:50 ET: metrics returned to baseline; customer reported improved throughput.

Deliverables:
- Postmortem draft (will link to DRIVE and INC ticket).
- Executive timeline and comms for the customer's execs.
- One-time credit: 10% to be applied to July invoice (as approved by Rishi).

I'll follow up with the postmortem link in the next email.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
